elements.element: Customer shall not be required to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2 continues to require the Company to pay the Termination Payment, and the added sentence expressly characterizes it as a “liquidated amount” and “liquidated damages.”

elements.element: Customer shall not be required to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: The Company remains obligated to pay the Termination Payment, and the added sentence expressly identifies that payment as the only “penalty payable by the Company,” leaving one penalty payable.

elements.element: Any termination fee payable by Customer shall be triggered only by Customer's early termination of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The operative trigger remains whenever “the Company terminates this Agreement.” It is not limited to termination before the end of the term and does not exclude other Company-initiated terminations.

elements.element: The early-termination fee payable by Customer shall not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The added sentence caps the Termination Payment at the fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three months preceding the Termination Date.

elements.element: The early-termination fee shall be the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the Termination Payment is the only liquidated amount, liquidated damages, or penalty payable by the Company under the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it preserves a stipulated payment and expressly labels it as liquidated damages or a penalty. It adds the fallback cap and exclusivity language, but it does not limit the payment trigger to early termination; it remains applicable whenever the Company terminates. Thus neither complete level is satisfied. The added cap otherwise integrates without disturbing unrelated terms or creating a direct contradiction.
